purpose.p: What Publish writes to the release bucket, how a site server reads it and answers visitors, and how rollback, maintenance, private sites and private links work.

list.item: A release bucket with S3 versioning, written by websites and read by site servers with read-only keys.
The site's root page with a public origin: it is the site's address.

step.title: What Publish writes
step.p: Publish renders each selected page in each selected language and writes one zip object per page and language, then the site index, then the bindings. Every write is a new S3 version: nothing is overwritten in place.

row.cell: The page in the main language.
The site index: for every page and language, its URL, object key, the S3 version online, fingerprint, assets, refresh time, whether it is indexable and its language; the redirects; maintenance.
Public origin → site id and state (public or private), for every site.

step.p: A page object holds page.json (the page Bag, URL, fingerprint, the SHA-256 of the HTML, language), index.html (the pre-rendered page), its assets by content address, and for a page whose Data uses resolvers request.json, the render request without connections. The index is written after the pages and pins their versions, so a reader never sees half a publication.

A page is selected when its fingerprint differs from the one online: name, URL, the page as its language sees it, effective SEO, site texts and the site's languages. A translation changes only its own language.

step.title: How a site server answers
step.p: A site server reads bindings.json and each site's index at most every cache interval, keeping the last valid ones, so a new address or a new publication needs no restart. For a request it finds the site by origin, then:

list.item: a private site answers 404 and a site in maintenance 503, unless the browser holds the cookie of a valid private link;
/robots.txt and /sitemap.xml come from the index; the sitemap lists every indexable page in every language; a root page that is not indexable closes the whole site to robots;
a redirect source answers 301 to its target, a path without its final slash 301 to the slashed one, a path with the main language's prefix 301 to the path without it;
/_assets/<sha256>.<ext> answers the asset with an immutable cache header;
a page URL answers its HTML; a page with resolvers is rendered again by the worker when its refresh time has passed and kept in a local cache;
anything else answers the 404 page of the path's language, else the main one.

step.p: Public pages carry no cookie and no session; only the private link sets one.

list.item: A page in one language: page_rollback pins an earlier S3 version of its object in a new index; the other pages and languages stay as they are.
The whole site: site_rollback restores a saved source version and publishes every page that differs from it.

step.title: Maintenance, private sites and private links
step.p: maintenance_set writes a new index with the maintenance flag; pages stay as they are. site_visibility_set makes the site private or public at its address, even before the first Publish.

private_link returns <address>/_private/<token>, valid 8 hours or 7 days. The token names the site and its expiry and is signed with HMAC-SHA256 under a secret shared by websites and the site servers. Opening it sets an HttpOnly cookie for that host (Secure on https, SameSite=Lax) and redirects to /; with it, the real site shows and its responses are not stored by shared caches. Rotating the secret revokes every link.

rule.why: Publish refuses an address that belongs to another site.

rules.rule: Give each site its own public origin.

rule.why: Pages are read by pinned version.

rules.rule: Give the site servers keys that can read object versions (GetObjectVersion, ListBucketVersions) and nothing else.

rule.why: A link works until it expires and cannot be revoked one by one.

rules.rule: Give private links the shortest validity that serves.

limits.limit: An index of an earlier schema reads as absent: the next Publish writes every page again; until then the site server answers 503 for that site.
A site server serves the sites of one release bucket; there is no registry of servers yet.

facts.fact: The page object and index schema is 3; entries carry language.
The main language's entry is the page id; another language's is <page>.<language>.
Publish writes the pages, then the index, then the binding of the site's address.
A translation changes the fingerprint of its own language only.
A running site server serves an address set after it started and stops serving the old one.
The main language's prefixed path answers 301 to the unprefixed one.
The sitemap lists indexable pages of every language; a noindex root gives Disallow: /.
Private links last 8 or 168 hours; forged, foreign and expired tokens are refused.
A valid private link answers 303 with an HttpOnly cookie for its host.
The Docker composition publishes the example site in two languages, serves it, and opens it through a private link during maintenance.
